content.user_title: Verify Research and Facts for Authors
content.value_statement: Authors need accurate details without slowing the draft process. This skill structures research, checks claims, and turns findings into usable writing guidance.
actual_capabilities: Builds research briefs with questions, source types, and reliability checks.
Extracts factual claims from manuscript passages for verification.
Flags inaccuracies, anachronisms, unsupported claims, and weak source fit.
Suggests story-friendly revisions that preserve narrative flow.
Creates bibliography structures for books, articles, interviews, and expert notes.
Provides checklists for cross-referencing facts across independent sources.
limitations: It cannot guarantee truth without access to current and reliable sources.
It does not replace expert review for medical, legal, or cultural sensitivity topics.
It may need browsing or provided sources for recent facts.
It does not automatically retrieve or store source documents.

use_cases.title: Historical Fiction Detail Review
use_cases.description: Check scenes for period-accurate objects, language, social customs, and known events.

use_cases.title: Nonfiction Claim Verification
use_cases.description: Turn draft claims into a review list with source needs, confidence levels, and corrections.

use_cases.title: Science Fiction Plausibility Check
use_cases.description: Review speculative scenes against current science and suggest plausible alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Basic Research
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a research brief for my story topic. Include key questions, source types, red flags, and a note template.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Fact-check this passage for accuracy. List verified claims, questionable claims, errors, and suggested revisions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Source Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a source strategy for this manuscript topic. Separate primary sources, secondary sources, experts, and reliability checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Manuscript Section
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this chapter for factual risk. Prioritize fixes by reader impact, cite source needs, and propose narrative-safe corrections.

output_examples.input: A novelist asks what to research for an American art student in 1920s Paris.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a research brief with art schools, housing, transportation, social context, source types, and anachronism checks.

output_examples.input: A science fiction writer submits a paragraph about walking outside on Mars without a suit.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies pressure, temperature, radiation, and visibility issues, then suggests plausible revised scene options.

output_examples.input: An editor needs source tracking for a nonfiction chapter.
output_examples.output: The skill provides a bibliography structure with source type, publication date, reliability, key information, and follow-up needs.

best_practices: Provide the genre, time period, location, and intended accuracy level before asking for research.
Ask for source reliability notes when facts affect plot, character decisions, or reader trust.
Keep a bibliography while drafting so every important detail remains traceable.
anti_patterns: Do not accept unsupported facts when the scene depends on technical or historical accuracy.
Do not use research as exposition when it can appear through action, conflict, or dialogue.
Do not rely on one source for claims that could affect safety, culture, or public reputation.

faq.question: Does this skill browse the web by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides research structure and verification workflow unless the host assistant has browsing tools enabled.

faq.question: Can it verify recent facts?
faq.answer: Yes, but recent facts require current sources or browsing support. Ask it to cite publication dates.

faq.question: Is it only for historical fiction?
faq.answer: No. It also supports nonfiction, science fiction, cultural details, professions, and technical topics.

faq.question: Can it replace an expert consultant?
faq.answer: No. Use qualified experts for specialized, sensitive, legal, medical, or culturally specific material.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: Give the passage, setting, target reader, desired realism level, and any sources already used.

faq.question: Can it help reduce info-dumps?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests ways to integrate facts through character action, sensory detail, conflict, and dialogue.
